function.name: exec_command
function.description: Run a shell command. Returns output and status; a running session_id can be polled with write_stdin. background starts a tracked job; detach starts a lasting service when permitted. Linux sandbox jobs have private loopback: run servers and clients together. Residual processes stop on return. Create and edit files with shell commands. One command may write files and run the check together.

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in ms; normally yields a running session, or stops it when hard timeout is configured.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait in ms before returning output and any running session_id.

sandbox_permissions.description: Use require_escalated only when the permission policy allows requesting approval.

additional_permissions.description: Additional sandbox permissions requested for this call.

justification.description: Why the requested permission is needed.

prefix_rule.description: Optional reusable command prefix for an approval.

function.name: write_stdin
function.description: Poll session_id with empty chars, or send input (requires an initial tty=true). Include input newlines. Input uses the session's sandbox_permissions.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait in ms before returning output and any running session_id.

sandbox_permissions.description: Use require_escalated only when the permission policy allows requesting approval.

additional_permissions.description: Additional sandbox permissions requested for this call.

justification.description: Why the requested permission is needed.

function.name: kill_process
function.description: Stop this conversation's exec sessions: session_id, session_ids, or all=true. Never find processes to kill by matching command text or file names.

function.name: FileRead
function.description: Read a text file, an image, PDF pages or a notebook. offset is 1-based; limit counts lines (default 2000). PDFs over 10 pages need pages (at most 20). Reads authorize edits; a file listing does not.

pages.description: PDF page range, for example 1-5; at most 20 pages.
